text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 4% today as oil prices climbed on Middle East supply concerns and diesel stayed tight. The IEA warned that diesel shortages will persist into 2027 due to Iran war disruptions and falling inventories, while Saudi officials reported attacks on Aramco facilities—news that pushed crude prices higher. For a refiner like Marathon, tighter diesel supplies and higher crude costs can improve refining margins (the profit from turning crude into finished fuel), especially when diesel commands premium prices due to scarcity.

The stock's 22% surge over two weeks reflects a broader shift: traders have moved from worrying about Russian diesel flooding the market (which would cheapen fuel) to focusing on Middle East supply risks and sustained tight conditions. With U.S. refineries running at 92.7% capacity and diesel inventories lean at 105 million barrels, the refiner can push higher margins as long as demand holds and supply stays constrained.
